title.narrative: Flood affected families have access to dignified basic shelter/NFI services in IDP in Galkacyo south district Mudug region.

description.narrative: ltpgtThe proposed project is a life-saving intervention that aims to support flood-affected persons by improving their living conditions and forming the foundation to accelerate their recovery from associated shocks. The project targets 2700 households (16,200 persons) living in IDP sites in Galkacyo South district. The targeted flood-affected persons comprise of 5,184 women, 3,564 girls, 4,212 men and 3,240 boys living in twelve IDP sites. The targeted sites include:Halgan, Qoraxey, Gargar, Doxamudug, Mahaday, Karama, Midnimo, Bulo jawan, Bantu 3, Degaan, Takulo, Isxaq, Towfiq, and Bula ajuuran.ltspangt2700 non-food items and plastic sheets will be distributed to 2700 households (16,200 persons) to enable them have access to basic household utensils and shelter supporting materials. Each household will be supported with two pieces of plastic sheets to enable them re-establish shelter structures that were damaged and destroyed by the floods. The project aims to have an overall beneficiary reach of 2700 households (16,200 persons). The distributions of the items will be carried out in two phases. The project staff will employ a highly participatory approach that is gender-sensitive and diversity cognizant in the implementation of activities. This will include community mobilization/sensitization, targeting/beneficiary selection, registration and verification, cash transfers, monitoring. The NFIs and plastic sheets will be distributed in two phases. lt/spangtltspangtTwo post distribution monitoring exercises will be conducted for the two distribution phases. The PDM exercises are aimed at understanding the effectiveness of processes employed, acquire beneficiary feedback on the reception of their entitlements, quality and quantity of items, utilisation of the items, levels of satisfaction, satisfaction with the modality of delivering aid and other important aspects to support the project's informed decision making. lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtTo enhance accountability to the affected persons, the project will adequately invest in complaints, feedback and response mechanisms. Two CFRM desks and a toll-free number will be established to facilitate community engagement and promote reception of feedback and responses during the project's implementation. The CFRM desks will be strategically placed in the targeted IDP sites and will be operational for the working hours of the day. The hotline number will equally be operational for the day's working hours to accommodate those who would not be comfortable with giving feedback through the desks. The hotlines will also enhance anonymity in the entire CFRM system. lt/pgtltpgtThe project will coordinate efforts with other humanitarian actors operating in the same area and seek complementarity where feasible to stimulate synergy. These will ensure targeted beneficiaries have access to a holistic response that addresses their most pressing needs. Service referral pathways and complementarity efforts will lay the foundation for a sustainable project that supports the flood-affected communities to graduate through the process of recovering from shocks, rebuilding the livelihoods and returning to normalcy. To realise this, the project will closely work with all stakeholders such as the community leadership, local administration agencies, humanitarian and development agencies such as IOM, NRC in scaling up the coordination efforts in supporting the flood affected population in Galkacyo South. Sites selected was done in coordination with the representative from the local authorities and they were not supported by IOM and NRC. lt/pgt
